reason: The text presents multiple emphatic hierarchical structures: divine authority (YHWH commands Moses and controls Pharaoh's heart), mediatory authority (Moses relays God's commands to the Israelites), organized military hierarchy (Pharaoh's chariots, horsemen, and army), and collective subordination (the Israelites as a unified group under leadership). These hierarchical relationships are not incidental but central to the narrative—the text repeatedly emphasizes chains of command (God → Moses → Israelites) and organizational authority (Pharaoh's military structure). The underlying theological assertion that God stands above all actors reinforces a cosmic hierarchy as foundational to the events described.
